In addition to releasing the public beta 2 of macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, Apple today also started rolling out the first release candidate of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2. Details below.

Older versions of macOS continue to receive security updates

As is customary for major updates of older macOS versions, Apple today directly released the first release candidate of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 without first rolling out regular beta versions.

Apple previously released macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 at the end of last month, and both versions went through two release candidates before their official release.

The release notes provided by Apple for the first release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 only mention that both "provide important security fixes and are recommended for all users to install." Last month's update included a CoreGraphics security fix, which reads:

Apple is expected to disclose the details of the fixes only after the official release of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.2, and these two versions will most likely be officially released within the next few weeks, alongside macOS 27.2 Golden Gate.

The build number of release candidate 1 of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 is 24H219, while the build number of release candidate 1 of macOS Tahoe 26.7.2 is 25G320.

Have you found anything new or different in this release candidate? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
